strategies.overview:
Flying

Iron Jugulis separates itself from Flying's other special attacking threats thanks to an extremely diverse movepool and superior Speed, allowing it to reliably deal with Steel- and Ghost-types. However, it can often come up short of KOs, and Flying has several other fast and strong special attackers like Enamorus and Landorus that offer more vital immunities and superior power at the cost of Speed, while Tornadus-T, while weaker, packs a far more valuable Speed stat and longevity with Regenerator.

movesets.name: Choice Specs (Flying)
movesets.description:
Iron Jugulis finds a niche on Flying teams as a capable Choice Specs user thanks to is solid Speed and Special Attack enabling it to outpace and remove targets such as Gholdengo and Urshifu-R. Dark Pulse nails problematic Psychic- and Ghost-types such as Iron Crown, Ceruledge, and Gholdengo. Hurricane takes out Fighting- and Fairy-types like Okidogi and Primarina that could take on Dark Pulse. Fire Blast provides great coverage, enabling Iron Jugulis to beat Steel-types such as Corviknight and Iron Treads. Alternatively, Focus Blast allows Iron Jugulis to OHKO Kyurem and 2HKO Hisuian Goodra. Finally, Earth Power deals with Rock- and Fire-types like Glimmora, Hisuian Arcanine, and Heatran.

Corviknight serves a crucial teammate, being able to safely pivot in Iron Jugulis with U-turn along with using Defog to remove Stealth Rock. Corviknight's Steel typing also lets it take on Fairy- and Ice-types that threaten Iron Jugulis such as Enamorus, Alolan Ninetales, and Articuno. Skarmory can take on physical Ice- and Rock-types like Weavile and Iron Boulder with its high Defense and Body Press. Gliscor easily takes on problematic Electric-types like Regieleki and Sandy Shocks while reliably beating down special walls such as Hisuian Goodra. Gliscor can also provide Stealth Rock to wear down checks like Assault Vest Tornadus-T and Assault Vest Iron Hands. Choice Scarf Landorus-T can similarly handle Electric-types like Raging Bolt along with dealing with Fire-types like Gouging Fire and Cinderace. Choice Scarf Enamrous provides a fast special attacker capable of removing faster threats like Choice Specs Greninja, Darkrai, and Choice Specs Dragapult while appreciating Iron Jugulis majorly hindering special walls like Hisuian Goodra and Clodsire. Enamorus can also use Healing Wish to heal Iron Jugulis back up in important matchups such as Ghost and Psychic if takes too much damage. Dragonite appreciates Iron Jugulis removing physical walls like Galarian Weezing, Sableye, and Forretress while being able to use Extreme Speed to pick of faster targets like Meowscarada and Latios that would otherwise beat Iron Jugulis. Assault Vest Tornadus-T can take on special attackers like Iron Moth and opposing Iron Jugulis while providing Knock Off to cripple bulky targets like opposing Assault Vest Tornadus-T and Alolan Muk. Moltres provides support through burn to chip down foes like specially defensive Corviknight and Articuno along with dealing with physical attackers like IronPress Zamazenta and Sneasler.

movesets.name: Booster Energy
movesets.description:
• While not quite as powerful or versatile as its counterpart Hydreigon, Iron Jugulis fills a unique role due to its higher Speed and Flying-type STAB.

  • Hurricane vs Air Slash: Hurricane secures KOs on Pokemon like Iron Bundle that Air Slash cannot, however, Air Slash is much less likely to miss, and the flinch chance can come in handy occasionally.

  • Taunt: With Taunt, Iron Jugulis stops walls such as Clodsire from healing off its attacks, and prevents debilitating status that would otherwise cut its sweep short.

  • Earth Power: Earth Power grants Iron Jugulis valuable coverage on most Pokémon that would not mind its main attacks, like Tinkaton.

  • Flash Cannon: Flash Cannon is useful for hitting Fairy-types such as Flutter Mane for big damage.

  • Flamethrower: Flamethrower provides super effective coverage on Steel-types that might otherwise cause issues for Iron Jugulis.

Other Options

  • Knock Off: While not doing much damage to many does due to Iron Jugulis's thoroughly average Attack stat, Knock Off can still help Iron Jugulis and its teammates by softening up defensive cores via item removal.

  • Substitute: Substitute can be used to punish Spore attempts from the likes of Breloom and Brute Bonnet, as well as easing prediction by scouting switches.

  • Focus Blast: Though unreliable due to its accuracy, Focus Blast is Iron Jugulis's best option to hit Kingambit.

Tera Types

  • Flying: Terastallizing into a Flying-type boosts Iron Jugulis's damage output with Air Slash and Hurricane, making it even more difficult to switch into while removing the weaknesses that come from its secondary Dark typing.

  • Dark: A Dark-type Tera boosts Dark Pulse's damage considerably, and when coupled with its rather high flinch rate, a Tera Dark Iron Jugulis can prove quite difficult to handle for some teams.

  • Steel: A Steel-type Tera grants Iron Jugulis a resistance to Fairy and Ice, improving its matchup with Flutter Mane and Iron Bundle and giving it STAB on Flash Cannon.

  • Ground: Tera Ground gives Iron Jugulis an Electric-type immunity, allowing it to block Volt Switch from the likes of Rotom-W and Iron Hands while also giving it STAB on Earth Power.

movesets.name: NANO LOVE (Choice Item)
movesets.description:
• With its good Speed and powerful STABs, Iron Jugulis lends itself nicely to use a Choice item set, setting itself apart from Hydreigon by virtue of its higher Speed at the cost of some power.

  • Hurricane vs Air Slash: Hurricane offers Iron Jugulis an extremely powerful Flying-type STAB attack, though Air Slash is far more consistent due to its higher accuracy.

  • Earth Power: Earth Power allows Iron Jugulis to hit otherwise irritating switch-ins like Magnezone and Tinkaton.

  • Flash Cannon: Flash Cannon allows Iron Jugulis to punish Fairy-type switch-ins such as Flutter Mane, as well as the numerous Tera Fairy users in the BSS metagame.

  • U-turn: U-turn allows Iron Jugulis to keep momentum for its team by scouting switches and pivoting out of disadvantageous matchups.

Items

  • Choice Specs: Choice Specs elevates Iron Jugulis's power, allowing it to wallbreak much more consistently.

  • Choice Scarf: Choice Scarf's Speed boost allows Iron Jugulis to outspeed otherwise faster foes like Flutter Mane and Iron Bundle, potentially surprising them with early KOs.

Tera Types

  • Flying: Tera Flying boosts Air Slash to more respectable power levels, and also makes Hurricane incredibly hard to switch into safely.

  • Dark: Tera Dark pushes Dark Pulse's damage output even further, making Iron Jugulis very hard to deal with in conjunction with the move’s ever-irritating flinch rate.

  • Steel: Tera Steel gives Iron Jugulis resistances to Fairy and Ice, improving its matchup against Flutter Mane and Iron Bundle.

strategies.overview:
• Iron Jugulis's great type combination and access to strong support moves such as Tailwind and Snarl make it a niche but powerful disruptive threat. With Booster Energy, Iron Jugulis is able to outspeed almost every other Pokemon in the format and use its great support options to apply pressure on the opponent with fast Snarls and Air Slashes. Its typing gives it an immunity to Prankster Taunt, as well as resistances to attacks from several common threats such as Rillaboom's Wood Hammer and Urshifu-S's Wicked Blow.

  • Iron Jugulis is used on semi-Trick Room teams with Farigiraf and Ursaluna-B, as it forces opponents to respect both a potential Tailwind from Iron Jugulis and Trick Room from Farigiraf. Both Incineroar and Ogerpon-W are great partners for Iron Jugulis; Incineroar provides Fake Out support and weakens potential threats such as Chien-Pao with Intimidate, and Ogerpon-W provides redirection to allow Iron Jugulis to set up Tailwind more easily. Flutter Mane also forms a very strong and consistent pairing with Iron Jugulis, countering opposing Dark-types that Iron Jugulis would have trouble dealing with.

  • While having a few strong resistances, Iron Jugulis's typing also means it's weak to common metagame threats such as Flutter Mane, especially the Speed Booster Energy variants, and Chien-Pao, which threaten an OHKO. Iron Jugulis also struggles against Pokemon that resist its STAB moves and can take advantage of its low damage output like Incineroar and Raging Bolt. Additionally, Iron Jugulis struggles to find a place on most teams due to it competing with Tornadus, which, unlike Iron Jugulis, has access to Prankster Tailwind, a strong Flying-type STAB move in the form of Bleakwind Storm, and Prankster Rain Dance and Sunny Day.

movesets.name: Tailwind Support
movesets.description:
• Snarl is helpful to slow down the plethora of strong special attackers in the format.

  • Booster Energy allows Iron Jugulis to fire off fast attacks like Snarl into opposing special attackers and set up Tailwind more easily, as well as outspeed threats such as Chien-Pao.

  • The bulk allows Iron Jugulis to survive a Extreme Speed from Choice Band Tera Normal Dragonite with Sword of Ruin active, as well as an Icicle Crash from a -1 Attack Chien-Pao. After a Snarl, Iron Jugulis lives a Dazzling Gleam from Choice Specs Tera Fairy Flutter Mane, as well as Thunderbolt from Raging Bolt.

  • Both Tera Poison and Steel are viable, but Poison is generally preferred thanks to the Fighting resistance and generally better synergy with Iron Jugulis's original type. In comparison, Tera Steel gives more resistances to powerful moves in the format like Blood Moon and Make It Rain, but it is weak to more types than Tera Poison.

movesets.name: Booster Energy
movesets.description:
Iron Jugulis's combination of good support tools in Snarl and Tailwind, great offensive typing, and powerful Hurricane make it a versatile utility attacker that works well in rain. Snarl provides Iron Jugulis with a damage reduction option that not only supports its team but also gives it a favorable matchup against the likes of Calyrex-S and Terapagos. Hurricane's pairing with rain gives Iron Jugulis the ability to consistently threaten Pokemon like the Urshifu formes and Rillaboom. Tailwind is a strong speed control option to help support both itself and its teammates. The Speed investment along with Booster Energy allows Iron Jugulis to outspeed Choice Scarf Urshifu-R. The defensive investment allows Iron Jugulis to survive Flare Blitz from Koraidon in sun, Moonblast from non-Choice Specs Flutter Mane, and Thunderbolt from Assault Vest Raging Bolt. Tera Water provides Iron Jugulis with a better defensive typing against matchups like Calyrex-I and Urshifu-R.

Iron Jugulis typically struggles versus powerful Electric-types like Miraidon and Booster Energy Raging Bolt, both of which threaten to OHKO it. Urshifu-R can also be a somewhat problematic matchup, threatening huge damage under rain with Surging Strikes and forcing Iron Jugulis to Terastallize. Assault Vest Kyogre is Iron Jugulis's best partner, providing rain for its Hurricane and benefitting greatly from Iron Jugulis's Tailwind. Kyogre's superb special bulk allows it to become untouchable on the special side when paired with Snarl, and, with Tera Grass, it can reliably deal with Electric-type threats. Urshifu-R is another great partner, as both it and Iron Jugulis are strong weather abusers that appreciate weather control, with Iron Jugulis covering for the Grass-types that Urshifu-R typically struggles against. Urshifu-R is a great beneficiary of Tailwind, which allows it to fire off fast Surging Strikes next to Iron Jugulis to exert offensive pressure. Iron Jugulis also pairs well with Incineroar thanks to Intimidate + Snarl being a particularly strong damage-reducing combination to cover a multitude of threats alongside Fake Out, which allows Iron Jugulis to set up Tailwind safely.

movesets.name: Offensive Support
movesets.description:
Set Details

  • Iron Jugulis serves as a strong utility attacker on rain teams with its solid typing and great support options in Snarl and Tailwind. Iron Jugulis has good matchups into common Flying-weak Pokemon like Rillaboom, Ogerpon, and the Urshifu formes.
  • With the plethora of powerful special attackers in the format like Calyrex-S, Kyogre, Terapagos, and Lunala, Snarl acts as a consistent way to slow down these would-be sweepers and give opportunities to Iron Jugulis's team. Tailwind paired with Iron Jugulis's high Speed allows it to easily give its team the Speed advantage in front of much faster threats.
  • The defensive investment allows Iron Jugulis to live a Flare Blitz from Koraidon, Moonblast from Focus Sash Flutter Mane, or Volt Switch from Miraidon after a Snarl. The Speed investment paired with Booster Energy allows Iron Jugulis to outspeed Calyrex-S and Choice Scarf Urshifu-R.
  • Tera Steel provides Iron Jugulis a strong defensive typing in rain while also giving key resistances to Ice- and Fairy-type moves like Icicle Crash from Chien-Pao and Moonblast from Flutter Mane. Tera Fire acts as a solid alternative, still providing resistances to Ice and Fairy but losing out on a multitude of other resistances and being a much weaker individual typing under rain. Even with these downsides, its lack of a Fighting weakness makes it better into certain matchups like Zamazenta-C and Iron Hands.

Teambuilding

  • Iron Jugulis typically struggles against strong Electric- and Ice-types like Miraidon and Calyrex-I that threaten to OHKO it. More defensive Pokemon that Iron Jugulis struggles to damage like Zamazenta-C and Grimmsnarl can also be difficult for it because they can ignore it without many repercussions.
  • Kyogre is Iron Jugulis's best partner, providing rain for Iron Jugulis's Hurricane while benefiting greatly from Tailwind and Snarl; Kyogre survives three Astral Barrages from Calyrex-S and lives Volt Switch from Miraidon after a Snarl. Zacian-C also functions as a great partner, covering for most of the aforementioned checks to Iron Jugulis as well as having the ability to outspeed Choice Scarf Miraidon with Tailwind. These Pokemon also cover well for the Calyrex-I matchup, resisting Glacial Lance and firing off strong and consistent damage into it.
  • Grass-types such as Amoonguss and Rillaboom work well with Iron Jugulis, providing Rage Powder and Fake Out, respectively, to give Iron Jugulis the opportunity to set up Tailwind while covering the problematic Miraidon matchup. Amoonguss also provides solid defensive coverage against threats like Zamazenta-C, resisting its Body Press and either redirecting its attacks or threatening it with Spore. Urshifu-R is also a great partner for Iron Jugulis on rain teams, benefiting from the Speed boost to fire off powerful rain-boosted Surging Strikes that can bulldoze through said bulky threats that Iron Jugulis typically struggles against.

strategies.overview:
Draft Order: Round 6 onwards

Price Range: 7-8 points

Overview: Iron Jugulis has a solid Speed tier, access to Speed Booster Energy, a good typing, strong Flying STAB moves, and solid offensive coverage, making it a great cleaner. While its offensive versatility allows it to fulfill other roles if necessary, it tends to lack consistency and raw power. On top of that, it can be difficult to justify drafting a Pokemon that is primarily used as an endgame cleaner when most stronger Pokemon can also fulfill a cleaner role while benefitting the draft in other ways. Iron Jugulis is good at what it does, but many other Pokemon can also do its job equally well or better. These flaws keep it around the middle of the draft board, and it doesn't find itself drafted very often. On the bright side, Terastallization significantly helps Iron Jugulis and can turn it into a legitimate threat, giving it the consistency and power it craves, but the opportunity cost of Terastallizing it prevents it from being a popular pick.
strategies.comments:
Common Roles

Booster Energy Cleaner: Paired with Speed Booster Energy, Iron Jugulis outpaces the entire unboosted metagame and can sweep a weakened team with its strong STAB and coverage options. These sets may also utilize Taunt to deny recovery for foes not quite in KO range of Iron Jugulis's attacks.

Wallbreaker: By using a damage-boosting item and usually Tera Flying, Iron Jugulis can unleash very powerful Hurricanes to break through opposing walls with sheer power. These sets have their true damage potential limited by Hurricane's inconsistency, but Iron Jugulis has solid, accurate coverage options it can use if needed.

Offensive Pivot: Leveraging its good defensive typing and Speed, Iron Jugulis can find several opportunities to enter the field during battle and gain momentum with U-turn. These sets usually run Heavy-Duty Boots and can also make use of Knock Off and Taunt to disrupt defensive Pokemon. Alternatively, these sets can run Choice Scarf to act as solid speed control.

Common Moves

Primary STAB Moves: Hurricane, Air Slash, Dark Pulse

Setup Moves: Meteor Beam

Utility Moves: Knock Off, U-turn, Roar, Taunt, Dragon Tail

Coverage: Dragon Pulse, Earth Power, Fire Blast, Flamethrower, Flash Cannon, Focus Blast, Heat Wave, Hydro Pump, Tera Blast

Niche Moves

Acrobatics: While Iron Jugulis's Attack isn't very high, on Booster Energy sets, Acrobatics can sometimes be strong enough to be worth using as an accurate Flying STAB move without committing to Tera Flying Tera Blast.

Charge Beam: Charge Beam is one of the few options Iron Jugulis has to boost its Special Attack, so it can be used as an option to increase Iron Jugulis's damage output, particularly on Tera Electric sets.

Work Up: Work Up can be used as a reliable means to increase Iron Jugulis's Special Attack, but it's rare that its relatively limited damage output increase is advantageous compared to using a damage-boosting item.

Common Items

Booster Energy: Booster Energy is almost always used for the Speed boost, giving Iron Jugulis the capability to sweep late-game.

Heavy-Duty Boots: As Iron Jugulis is naturally weak to Stealth Rock, Heavy-Duty Boots is often useful to negate Stealth Rock's chip damage.

Damage-boosting Items: If Iron Jugulis wants to act as a wallbreaker, it can use items like Choice Specs, Life Orb, and Expert Belt to increase its damage output.

Niche Items

Choice Scarf: While Speed Booster Energy is usually preferred, Choice Scarf is better on Iron Jugulis sets that want to switch in multiple times in battle for more consistent speed control.

Power Herb: Power Herb is used in combination with Meteor Beam to give Iron Jugulis a way to boost its Special Attack while maintaining its damage output.

Resistance Berries: Iron Jugulis's passable bulk and decent coverage allow it to occasionally act as a lure with a resistance Berry.

Tera

Iron Jugulis is typically drafted as a secondary Tera Captain, and it makes for a solid one. It normally uses a Tera type like Tera Fire, Steel, or Ground to boost one of its coverage moves, but it can also opt for basically any Type type depending on the matchup. It can opt for Tera Flying or Dark to boost its regular STAB attacks, or it can choose from Tera types such as Tera Electric and Fairy to gain coverage it normally does not have access to. The main downside of making Iron Jugulis a Tera Captain is opportunity cost. It is heavily elevated by Tera, but matchups where Iron Jugulis is a better choice to Terastallize in battle than the primary Tera Captain are few and far between.

Draft Strategy

Iron Jugulis is usually found on more offensive teams for its Speed tier and sweeping potential, but it does not provide much utility to a draft and isn't that strong without a damage-boosting item, so it requires a lot of support from its teammates. With that said, it is typically only drafted when its needed support options happen to already be fulfilled on the draft.

Entry Hazard Setters / Control: Iron Jugulis excels at sweeping a weakened team, and entry hazard support from Pokemon like Garchomp, Gliscor, and Glimmora makes it much easier to achieve this in battle. On the other hand, Iron Jugulis appreciates hazard removal from Pokemon like Great Tusk, Iron Treads, and Donphan, as it is weak to Stealth Rock and likes to use items besides Heavy-Duty Boots.

Physical Wallbreakers: Iron Jugulis struggles with specially bulky Pokemon, so it needs the support of a physical wallbreaker such as Palafin, Scizor, or Iron Hands to pressure and break through special walls.

Knock Off Users: Entry hazards greatly enable Iron Jugulis, but Heavy-Duty Boots can negate their impact. Iron Jugulis can use Knock Off itself, but it appreciates Knock Off support from Pokemon like Ogerpon, Tinkaton, and Galarian Zapdos to remove foes' Heavy-Duty Boots.

Alternate Speed Control: Iron Jugulis's Speed is good, but it's not great, so it fails to majorly contest the boosted metagame. It should be on teams that include a faster Pokemon such as Sneasler, Deoxys-S, or Cinderace so Iron Jugulis isn't solely relied on for speed control.

Checks and Counters

Faster Choice Scarf Users: Iron Jugulis unfortunately does not have a premier Speed tier, leaving it prone to being revenge killed by a faster Choice Scarf user such as Darkrai, Meowscarada, or Greninja when running its Speed Booster Energy sets.

Specially Defensive Walls: Iron Jugulis isn't really strong enough to break through specially defensive walls like Ting-Lu, Clefable, and Empoleon on its own, especially since it often doesn't use a damage-boosting item. Without a super effective Tera type, Iron Jugulis can struggle to find 2HKOs.
